argument:
The bull properly concedes that EPS declining from 2.11 to 1.99 sen defeats an achieved per-share growth claim. Margin improvement to 12.2% and a RM2.371bn book still support future project earnings, but that opportunity must outweigh ownership dilution rather than simply increase total profit. This is the distinction most relevant at 48x trailing earnings.

March RM32.112m simple FCF is genuine positive funding evidence, yet associate/JV and investment-property outlays exceeded that surplus and equity-related proceeds reached RM386.821m. Those dated balances cannot establish June liquidity. The higher operating margin answers project profitability, not whether retained cash and future earnings compensate enlarged share supply. Overbought price action adds chase risk. I oppose paying the growth premium for currently falling EPS and external expansion funding, without alleging that backlog delivery has failed.
key_points: Project margins and order book provide a credible growth runway.
Observed EPS dilution weakens shareholder participation.
Growth-priced entry must outweigh funding and investment demands.
rebuttal_to_previous: The bull answers project-level profitability but concedes the per-share counterexample. At 48x earnings, a future promise to outgrow dilution is weaker compensation than delivered EPS and post-expansion cash.
